fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The skeptic who went to India to disprove astrology", "body": "Emily Ridout tells Chance Garton that she first met astrology thirteen or fourteen years ago in India, where she had gone on a study abroad program and later worked teaching at a music conservatory. She was shocked when practitioners read specific medical detail out of a birth chart, including the exact month a woman's first period began, so she set out to disprove the whole system. She recounts reading a very fit fellow yoga trainee's chart, telling him it said he had weak ankles, and learning that his ankles were exactly where he kept getting injured. Anyone who fights a wisdom tradition, she says, loses."}, {"title": "Why the cosmos behaves like a chord", "body": "Chance asks how music and astrology connect, and Emily points to the quadrivium, number in time and number in space. When you sing a note well, overtones appear above it, and some singing traditions teach you to pop those overtones out. She argues the planetary movements are one partly visible depiction of the harmonic resonance of the universe, and because that universe is a fractal, we carry the same resonance inside our forms. Chance suggests the outer planets we cannot see are like the frequencies beyond hearing. Emily calls it the universe as a mirror with no originating image."}, {"title": "Solar and lunar principles inside the body", "body": "Emily separates two schools of yoga, one holding that manifest reality is made of light and one holding it is made of sound, and notes that mantra yogis start with the energy body while asana yogis start with the physical. She then unpacks the luminaries. The lunar principle is the subconscious builder, the intelligence that digests food, grows a child and carries memory including the Akashic record. The solar is the superconscious. She ties this to Ishvara Pranidhana in Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, the surrender that lets the higher principle take over, and to the koshas, the layers of individuated consciousness."}, {"title": "Samskaras, suffering and the mechanics of letting go", "body": "Chance asks where the grace to release something actually comes from. Emily answers that people stay in needless suffering because they are addicted to something that rides along with it, so the first move is to stop numbing with drugs, alcohol or excessive television, then sit in a quiet space and feel the sensation without mental attachment until it runs out. She says pain never lasts more than four minutes, though it returns. She frames this through samskaras, the latent seeds that burn off in practice, and recommends David Hawkins and his book Letting Go. Chance adds that the body is always doing its best option."}, {"title": "Building an actual astro yoga practice", "body": "Emily outlines three uses of astro yoga: practicing with the present sky, practicing with your own natal chart, and combining both through transits, such as Pluto crossing your ascendant. A reader can start simply, taking a troubled Aries placement and doing rabbit pose or a headstand daily, or go deeper by tracing a T square through signs, chakras and elements using the koshic model. She gives home students roughly six poses for ten minutes each morning. Gemini, she notes, rules the lungs, nervous system and arms. Start where the planets actually are, she says, beginning with sun and moon."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Emily Ridout returns to InnerVerse to debut her first book, AstroYoga For An Aquarian Age, a text that will help you combine astrology and yoga to embody your unique purpose. We will dive into the theory and practice of AstroYoga, to help us enter into a deeper connection with the cosmos as template for the human form, which is the mirror to the entire universe.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension our conversation takes us to mantras and the technology of language, the history of astrology, yoga, and ancient civilizations, the trinity and Linga/Yoni cults, reconciling sidereal and tropical systems, the spiral of large cycles of time, and much more.
